results.question: Can you list all tables in the SQLite database catalog?
results.sql: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'

results.question: which table stores customer's orders
results.sql: SELECT t FROM invoices AS t JOIN customers AS c ON t.CustomerId = c.CustomerId

results.question: How many customers are there
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customers.CustomerId) FROM customers

results.question: what are the top 5 countries that customers come from?
results.sql:
SELECT 
  COUNT(DISTINCT t2.Country) AS num_customers,
  t2.Country
FROM 
  invoices
JOIN 
  customers t1 ON invoices.CustomerId = t1.CustomerId
JOIN 
  employees t2 ON t1.SupportRepId = t2.EmployeeId
GROUP BY 
  t2.Country
ORDER BY 
  COUNT(DISTINCT t2.Country) DESC
LIMIT 5

results.question: List all albums and their corresponding artist names
results.sql: SELECT albums.Title AS AlbumTitle, artists.Name AS ArtistName FROM albums TO artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId

results.question: Find all tracks with a name containing "What" (case-insensitive)
results.sql: SELECT t.Name FROM tracks t JOIN invoice_items ii ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId JOIN invoices i ON ii.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId WHERE LOWER(t.Name) LIKE '%what%'

results.question: Get the total number of invoices for each customer
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(invoices.InvoiceId) AS TotalInvoicesPerCustomer FROM customers JOIN invoices ON customers.CustomerId = invoices.CustomerId GROUP BY customers.CustomerId

results.question: Find the total number of invoices per country:
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(c.Country) FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Country

results.question: List all invoices with a total exceeding $10:
results.sql: SELECT DISTINCT i.InvoiceId, i.Total FROM invoices AS i JOIN invoice_items AS ii ON i.InvoiceId = ii.InvoiceId WHERE ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity > 10

results.question: Find all invoices since 2010 and the total amount invoiced:
results.sql: SELECT invoices.InvoiceId, SUM(invoices.Total) AS TotalInvoiced FROM invoices WHERE invoices.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' GROUP BY invoices.InvoiceId

results.question: List all employees and their reporting manager's name (if any)
results.sql:
SELECT 
    e2.LastName AS Manager,
    e1.FirstName AS Employee,
    COALESCE(e2.Title, 'No Manager') AS Title
FROM 
    employees e1
LEFT JOIN 
    employees e2 ON e1.ReportsTo = e2.EmployeeId

results.question: Get the average invoice total for each customer
results.sql: SELECT invoices.Total / COUNT(DISTINCT customers.CustomerId) AS avg_invoice_total FROM invoices JOIN customers ON invoices.CustomerId = customers.CustomerId

results.question: Find the top 5 most expensive tracks (based on unit price)
results.sql:
SELECT 
    t.Name AS TrackName,
    t.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
    CONCAT(m.Name, ' ', t.GenreId) AS Genre
FROM 
    tracks t
JOIN 
    media_types m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
ORDER BY 
    t.UnitPrice DESC
LIMIT 5

results.question: List all genres and the number of tracks in each genre:
results.sql: SELECT g.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.TrackId) FROM genres AS g JOIN tracks AS t ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY g.Name

results.question: Get all genres that do not have any tracks associated with them:
results.sql:
SELECT g.Name 
FROM genres g 
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId 
WHERE t.TrackId IS NULL 
GROUP BY g.Name

results.question: List all customers who have not placed any orders:
results.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT c.FirstName, c.LastName
FROM customers c 
JOIN invoices i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
WHERE i.InvoiceId IS NULL

results.question: There are 3 tables: artists, albums and tracks, where albums and artists are linked by ArtistId, albums and tracks are linked by AlbumId, Can you find the top 10 most popular artists based on the number of tracks
results.sql:
SELECT 
    b.Name AS 'Artist Name', 
    COUNT(DISTINCT tr.TrackId) AS Number of Tracks
FROM 
    albums a 
JOIN 
    artists b ON a.ArtistId = b.ArtistId 
JOIN 
    tracks tr ON a.AlbumId = tr.AlbumId 
GROUP BY 
    b.Name
ORDER BY 
    Number of Tracks DESC LIMIT 10

results.question: List all customers from Canada and their email addresses:
results.sql: SELECT DISTINCT customers.FirstName, customers.LastName, customers.Email FROM customers WHERE customers.Country = 'Canada'

results.question: Find the customer with the most invoices
results.sql: SELECT customers.FirstName, customers.LastName, COUNT(invoices.InvoiceId) FROM customers JOIN invoices ON customers.CustomerId = invoices.CustomerId GROUP BY customers.CustomerId ORDER BY COUNT(invoices.InvoiceId) DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: Find the customer who bought the most albums in total quantity (across all invoices)
results.sql:
SELECT customers.FirstName, customers.LastName 
FROM customers
JOIN invoice_items ON customers.CustomerId = invoice_items.InvoiceId
JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
GROUP BY customers.FirstName, customers.LastName 
ORDER BY SUM(invoice_items.Quantity) DESC 
LIMIT 1

results.question: Hint: album quantity is found in invoice_items, Find the top 5 customers who bought the most albums in total quantity (across all invoices):
results.sql:
SELECT 
    c.FirstName, 
    c.LastName,
    SUM(i.Quantity) AS AlbumQuantity
FROM 
    customers c
JOIN 
    employees e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
JOIN 
    invoice_items i ON e.EmployeeId = (SELECT ReportsTo FROM employees WHERE EmployeeId = e.EmployeeId)
GROUP BY 
    c.FirstName, c.LastName
ORDER BY 
    AlbumQuantity DESC
LIMIT 5

results.question: Find the top 5 customers who spent the most money overall, Hint: order total can be found on invoices table, calculation using invoice_items detail table is unnecessary
results.sql:
SELECT 
    c.FirstName,
    c.LastName,
    SUM(i.Total) AS total_spent
FROM 
    customers c
JOIN 
    invoices i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
GROUP BY 
    c.CustomerId
ORDER BY 
    total_spent DESC
LIMIT 5

results.question: Get all playlists containing at least 10 tracks and the total duration of those tracks:
results.sql:
SELECT 
    p.Name AS "Playlists Containing Tracks", 
    SUM(t.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS "Total Track Duration"
FROM 
    playlist_track pt
JOIN 
    tracks t ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
JOIN 
    playlists p ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
GROUP BY 
    p.Name
HAVING 
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.Name) >= 10

results.question: Identify artists who have albums with tracks appearing in multiple genres:
results.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT t3.Name AS artist_name 
FROM albums t1 
JOIN tracks t2 ON t1.AlbumId = t2.AlbumId
JOIN genres t3 ON t2.GenreId = t3.GenreId
GROUP BY t1.ArtistId HAVING COUNT(t2.GenreId) > 1
